````text
# Course workflow — issues, PRs, reviews, sprint deliverables

Course rules, not upstream Gitea ones. Source: the course site <https://csci-435-se.github.io/>
(Sprints pages and Glossary) and `docs/sprint0/standards.md`. Everyone on the team, and every AI
session, uses the formats below so all issues and PRs look the same. The GitHub templates in
`.github/` carry the same formats; if they ever disagree with this page, fix the template.

AI disclosure has its own page: `AI-ASSISTANCE.md`.

## Current sprint: Sprint 3

- **Dates:** Nov 3 – Nov 19, 2026. Everything pushed and merged by **Nov 19, 11:59 PM**, except
  the D7 check-in, due **Nov 12, 11:59 PM** together with at least one code PR of your own, open
  and ready for review or merged.
- **Focus:** testing, meaning how well the tests check what the code is supposed to do.
- **Points:** 100.
- **Zero rule:** no merged PR (D4), no sprint report (D8) or no release (D9) means **0 for the
  whole sprint**.
- **Carries forward:** anything the Sprint 3 page doesn't change comes from the Sprint 2 and
  Sprint 1 pages, and every Sprint 0 standard still applies.
- **Start early:** record the test baseline at the Sprint 2 tag (see D8), and get the mutation tool
  running on any existing file in your area (see D6) before your PRs are ready.

| # | Deliverable | Points | Who | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Sprint backlog: a `Sprint 3` milestone with every selected issue on it, each with a justified scope | 10 | Team | GitHub milestone |
| D2 | Requirements spec for each issue (formats below), spec-reviewed on the issue before coding | 20 | Individual | Issue body |
| D3 | At least one non-trivial design decision per issue, with **at least two alternatives** | 5 | Individual | Issue body |
| D4 | Code changes and PRs, each with `## Test Evidence` and `## Tech Debt` sections | 20 | Individual | PRs |
| D5 | AI logs | 5 | Individual | `ai-logs/sprint3/<github-username>/` |
| D6 | Mutation testing on one issue's PR (CSCI 535: two) | 15 | Individual | `docs/sprint3/mutation/` |
| D7 | Mid-sprint check-in, linking a code PR | 5 | Individual | `docs/sprint3/checkin/<github-username>.md` |
| D8 | Sprint report, with a Suite health section | 10 | Team | `docs/sprint3/report.md` |
| D9 | Release: tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s3` plus a GitHub release | 2 | Team | Tags / Releases |
| D10 | Reflection survey | 8 | Individual | Blackboard/Zulip link |

### Graded strictly this sprint

The Sprint 3 page lists these as the rules that cost the most points. Details are in the sections
named.

1. No merge without a teammate's approval on the PR's **latest commit** (Reviews, below).
2. A spec review comment on the issue that says what was checked (Spec review, under the issue
   formats).
3. Every code PR has `Closes #<N>`, and both the issue and the PR are on the `Sprint 3` milestone.
4. Real AI logs, linked from the issue (D5).
5. A Test Evidence table in every PR, with expected values not copied from the code's output
   (Pull request format).
6. Mutation testing with a tool, with before and after reports committed (Mutation testing (D6)).
7. The team introduces no new test failures. A skipped test or a disabled CI check needs a linked
   issue and a reason in a code comment (D8).
8. A sprint report that renders on GitHub and uses the Sprint 3 sections (D8).

### Deliverable notes

- **D1 load:** each CSCI 435 student owns at least 2 medium issues; each CSCI 535 student owns at
  least 2 medium and 1 small. Either load can be met with equivalent story points instead. Every
  issue has exactly **one** assignee. Unfinished Sprint 2 issues go into the backlog before new
  work. To drop one, write the reason on that issue. If the backlog is too thin to meet the load,
  find areas that still need work (features, improvements, test gaps, bugs) and write new issues
  for them the usual way.
- **D1 scope:** every issue states its scope (small or medium) and one or two sentences on why:
  which components it touches and how much change is expected. The instructor or TA may reclassify
  an issue whose scope is clearly overstated.
- **D1 hardening issues (optional):** one of your issues may be a hardening issue. See "Hardening
  issues" below.
- **D1 team feature:** the instructor or TA posts a larger feature for Sprints 3–4 as an issue and
  tells the team. Split it into sub-issues, each with one owner, its own spec (D2) and scope, linked
  to the feature issue and added to the `Sprint 3` milestone. Sub-issues count toward the load.
- **D2:** specs are written and spec-reviewed before coding starts. Features use the user story
  format; hardening issues use the bug report format when they fix a defect, otherwise the
  hardening task format.
- **D3:** each decision names at least two concrete alternatives and why one won; this is graded
  strictly. The site also accepts the decision in an issue comment or the PR description; the team
  keeps it in the issue body. Decisions that span issues go in `docs/sprint3/design.md`.
- **D4:** every PR description has the Test Evidence and Tech Debt sections (see "Pull request
  format"). Per-PR scores are combined across your PRs and scaled to 20.
- **D5:** conventions are in `ai-logs/README.md`. Logs hold the full prompts and output. Graded
  strictly this sprint: a session summary, paraphrased prompts, a share link, or tool output without
  the prompts that produced it is not a log. The link must open the log file itself, not a folder
  or another issue. The folder must exist even if no AI was used; in that case, post a comment
  saying so. The site accepts the link from the issue or the PR; the team keeps it in **issue
  comments only** (`AI-ASSISTANCE.md`).
- **D6:** see "Mutation testing (D6)" below.
- **D7:** about 100 words on each of: what you have implemented so far and what remains; one thing
  you learned about testing in the project; one risk to finishing by Nov 19 and what you will do
  about it. Link at least one **code PR you authored**, open and ready for review or merged, by Nov
  12. On time, substantive and with a PR linked scores 5; late, thin or no PR 3; missing 0.
- **D8:** graded on completeness, specificity, quality of evidence and the Suite health section;
  sections are in "Sprint report (D8) sections" below.
- **D9:** keep the base version (`v1.27.3-csci435-s2` → `v1.27.3-csci435-s3`). Tag **after the
  last Sprint 3 merge**, so the release matches the final `main`, and push the tag to origin. The
  release description summarizes the sprint's features, fixes and hardening work, not just the tag
  name.
- **Reviews:** nobody approves or merges their own PR. Request the review on GitHub and tell the
  reviewer on Zulip; reviewers respond (approve or request changes) within 24 hours, with
  substantive comments and the rubric, not a bare approval. A PR is merged only after a teammate
  approves its **latest commit**: any push after the approval, including merging `main` in, needs
  a new approval. Once approved, the author merges. Each student reviews at least one PR per
  sprint, and every teammate at least once per semester.
- **Extra credit:** up to 3 points per PR submitted to upstream Gitea that is accepted or under
  active review, and up to 2 points per bug report filed upstream that comes from your own testing
  and is confirmed by the maintainers by the time Sprint 4 is graded. Both at the instructor's
  discretion.

## Branches and commits

- Branches: `feat/issue-<N>-short-description`, `fix/issue-<N>-short-description` or
  `chore/short-description` (`STUDENTS.md`). One issue per branch.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits and end with the issue number:
  `feat(repo): show empty state on releases page (#17)`. Add an
  `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer when AI helped; never `Co-Authored-By` or
  `Signed-off-by` (`AGENTS.md`). A human approves every commit before it is made.

### Before each implementation: sync with main

Every new branch starts from an up-to-date `main`. AI sessions run this before writing any code:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git switch -c feat/issue-<N>-short-description
```

To pick up new work on `main` for a branch that already exists, **merge, don't rebase**. Rebasing
or squashing after review has started is not allowed (`docs/sprint0/standards.md`):

```bash
git fetch origin
git merge origin/main
```

Do this before opening the PR and again if `main` moves while it is in review. A merge pushed after
approval needs a new approval (see Reviews). Never merge another feature branch into yours.

### After merge: clean up

A PR is merged with a merge commit once its latest commit is approved, every review comment is
addressed and CI passes. Then:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git branch -d feat/issue-<N>-short-description               # local branch
git push origin --delete feat/issue-<N>-short-description    # or GitHub's "Delete branch" button
git fetch --prune                                            # drop stale remote-tracking refs
```

Also check that the issue closed (via `Closes #N`), that the issue and PR are on the sprint
milestone, and that the issue has its AI Assistance comment. Then run `specstory sync` and file the
session's log (see `ai-logs/README.md`).

## Issue format: feature (user story)

Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/user-story.yaml`. The user story must meet INVEST: Independent,
Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable.

```markdown
## User Story
As a <role>, I want <capability> so that <benefit>.

## User Scenario
<A short concrete walk-through: who, where in the UI, what they do, what they see.>

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given <state>, when <action>, then <observable result>.
- [ ] AC2: ...
- [ ] AC3: ...            (at least 3; each has a clear pass/fail result)

## Out of Scope
- <What this issue deliberately does not do.>

## Open Questions
- <Unresolved questions, or "None".>

## Design Decision
**Decision:** <what was chosen>
**Alternatives Considered:** <at least two concrete options, and why each lost>
**Rationale:** <why this one>
**Consequences:** <trade-offs, follow-up work, what it makes harder>

## Scope
small | medium | large, and matching `scope:` label
<One or two sentences on why: the components it touches and how much change you expect.>
```

## Issue format: bug report

Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug-report.yaml`. Also used by hardening issues that fix a
defect.

```markdown
## Observed Behavior
## Expected Behavior
## Steps to Reproduce
1. ...
## Additional Information
<Version or commit, browser/OS, logs, screenshots.>
## Design Decision
<Same four fields as above: Decision, Alternatives Considered, Rationale, Consequences.>
## Scope
<Same as above: size, label and one or two sentences on why.>
```

## Issue format: hardening task

No GitHub template; write it in a blank issue. Used by hardening issues that don't fix a defect,
such as a flaky test or a broken CI check (Sprint 3, D2).

```markdown
## Problem
<What is unreliable now, and how you know: failing test names, run counts, CI run links.>
## Goal
<What "fixed" means.>
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: ...
## Evidence of Fix
<Which evidence from the table below the fix will show.>
## Design Decision
<Same four fields as above.>
## Scope
<Same as above: size, label and one or two sentences on why.>
```

### Hardening issues

Work that makes the existing system more reliable rather than adding a feature. Good sources: the
D8 baseline run (failing or flaky tests, broken CI checks on `main`); the "Introduced" and
"Encountered" Tech Debt fields of Sprint 1 and Sprint 2 PRs; bugs found in reviews or after
merging; and the upstream issue tracker for the parts of Gitea the team works on. It is scoped like
any other issue and must include evidence that the problem is fixed:

| Kind | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Bug fix | A test that fails before the fix and passes after |
| Flaky test | The root cause, and repeated runs before and after the fix (e.g. 20 for a unit test, 10 for E2E) |
| Broken or missing CI check | Links to CI runs before and after the fix |
| Failing tests in the baseline | Pass/fail counts before and after, and the cause of each group of failures |

The site doesn't say where the evidence goes: plan it in the issue (Evidence of Fix, or Additional
Information for a bug), then post the results on the issue and in the PR's Test Evidence once the
fix is in. Regenerating snapshots, reformatting code, or silencing a check without fixing its cause
counts as small at most.

### Design Decision and spec review

- **Design Decision (D3):** fill it in once you've picked an approach, before opening the PR. Put
  a second decision under another `### Decision 2` heading. If a PR changes the decision, update
  the issue body.
- **Spec review (D2):** before coding starts, a teammate posts a review comment **on the issue**.
  Start it with `Spec reviewed` so it is easy to find. The layout is the reviewer's choice, but the
  comment must say what was checked:
  1. each acceptance criterion: clear and testable, naming any that aren't;
  2. the cases considered (e.g. empty input, errors, permissions) and whether the ACs cover them;
  3. whether the scope fits the stated size;

  and end with an approval, or the problems for the author to fix in the spec. `Looks good!` with
  nothing about what was checked does not count. An optional layout:

  ```markdown
  Spec reviewed — @reviewer-username

  **Acceptance criteria:** <clear and testable? which aren't, and why>
  **Cases considered:** <which cases, and whether the ACs cover them>
  **Scope:** <does it fit the stated size?>
  **Verdict:** Approved | Changes needed: <list>
  ```

## Pull request format

Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:

1. `Closes #<N>`, which links the issue and closes it on merge. Every code PR links its issue, and
   the PR goes on the `Sprint 3` milestone too.
2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.
4. **Test Evidence:** required from Sprint 3. It replaces the old "How it was tested" section.
   Every behaviour change still needs a new or updated test.

   ```markdown
   ## Test Evidence

   | Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | AC1: ... | ... | ... | ... |

   **Not tested automatically, and why:** [...]

   **AI-written tests:** [Which tests were written or modified by AI, and how you checked that their expected values are correct. If none, write "None."]
   ```

   - **One row per acceptance criterion** from the issue; for a bug report, the Expected Behavior.
     A PR that changes no product behaviour (e.g. a CI change) writes `N/A` and why.
   - **Test(s):** the test name, plus the file if not obvious. For a manual check, write `Manual:`
     followed by the steps and what you saw. An AC tested both ways lists both in the same row.
   - **Level:** `unit`, `integration`, `E2E` or `manual`.
   - **Source of expected value:** `AC`, `issue discussion`, `docs`, `upstream behavior`, or
     `other` (explain). **Never the current output of your own code:** a test whose expected value
     was copied from what the code returns cannot detect that the code is wrong.
````

```text
S6a. Apply a suggestion across several lines open ['enhancement', 'scope: small'] ['Jack-Donohue'] None None
### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: small` · Type: Feature · Part of #151 · Depends on #156 (S3, merged in #179) and #158 (S5)

As a PR author, I want to apply a reviewer's suggestion on a range of lines with one click, so
that multi-line feedback lands on my branch the same way single-line feedback does.

### User Scenario

Ana selects lines 18–22 of `main.go` and suggests replacing them with two lines (S5). Ben clicks
**Apply suggestion**, keeps the default message "Apply suggestion from @ana on main.go" and
confirms. The page reloads, and the PR has one more commit in which lines 18–22 are replaced by
Ana's two lines and nothing else in the file changed.

### Acceptance Criteria

Errors from the Apply POST are returned as in S3 (#156): HTTP 400 with the message shown on the
page, unless an AC says otherwise.

- [ ] AC1: Given a suggestion on lines L–M (S5) and a user who can push to the head branch, when
  they apply it, then exactly one commit is added that replaces lines L–M with the block's lines
  in order, matching S5 AC5's diff. No line before L or after M changes. The commit message
  follows S3 AC1 (default "Apply suggestion from @<reviewer> on <file>", editable).
- [ ] AC2: Given the block is empty or holds one blank line, when it is applied, then the commit
  deletes lines L–M, or replaces them with one blank line (S5 AC6, S3 AC12).
- [ ] AC3: Given any line in L–M (first, middle or last) differs at head from the line the
  suggestion was written against, or the file now has fewer than M lines, or it was deleted or
  renamed, when someone applies it, then nothing is committed and they see "This suggestion is
  outdated: the code changed since it was written."
- [ ] AC4: Given a range suggestion, then the Apply button is shown or hidden under the same
  conditions as a single-line one (S3 AC2, AC5, AC7, AC9), and a direct POST gets S3's responses:
  403 for a user who can't push, 400 "Suggestions can only be applied to an open pull request
  whose branch still exists." for a closed or merged PR, 400 "This branch has new commits since
  the page was loaded. Reload the page and try again." for a stale head, and `Cannot commit to
  protected branch "<branch>".` for a protected branch.
- [ ] AC5: Given a file with CRLF line endings or no final newline, including a range that ends
  on the last line, when a range suggestion is applied, then the new lines use the file's line
  ending and the file's final-newline state is unchanged (S3 AC11).
- [ ] AC6: Given a range suggestion whose block equals lines L–M, when applied, then nothing is
  committed and they see "This suggestion makes no changes to the code." (S3 AC10).
- [ ] AC7: Given a single-line suggestion, then applying it behaves exactly as before: S3's
  existing tests pass without changes.
- [ ] AC8: Given a range suggestion and a single-line suggestion in the same file that don't overlap, when both are applied in one batch (S6, #159), then the commit applies each exactly as AC1 and S3 AC1 would on their own. *Moved from #159 AC15.*

### Out of Scope

- Applying several suggestions in one commit (S6, #159), which reuses this.
- Recording "applied" (S4, #157) and the API (S7, #160).
- Re-anchoring a range whose lines moved but didn't change: it is refused as outdated, like S3.

### Open Questions

- None.

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Generalise S3's `applySuggestionToContent` in
`services/repository/files/suggestion.go` to replace lines start..end instead of one line, where
a single-line comment is the range [Line, Line], and check every line of the range against S5's
`Comment.RangeOriginalLines()` before replacing.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *A separate `applyRangeSuggestionToContent`.* Leaves S3's function untouched, but duplicates its
  CRLF, final-newline and outdated handling, so the two would drift apart.
- *Build a patch from S5's rendered diff and run `git apply` in a temp clone.* S3 already rejected
  this: fuzzy matching can land the change on the wrong lines, and it duplicates what
  `ChangeRepoFiles` does.

**Rationale:** One function keeps a single place for line-ending handling, and S3's tests become
the regression check for the one-line case (AC7).

**Consequences:** `applySuggestionToContent` gets a start line. S6 (#159) calls it per suggestion,
bottom-up, so a batch can hold ranges. A range that moved but didn't change is refused.

### Scope

small

### Scope Justification

One service function in `services/repository/files/suggestion.go` (range replace plus a range
outdated check) and S3's Apply attribute offered on range comments, with unit tests for AC1–AC3,
AC5 and AC6 and one integration case for AC4. No new route, UI or schema change.
```

````text
    78	func CanApplySuggestions(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, pr *issues_model.PullRequest) (string, error) {

    98		if err != nil {
    99			return "", err

   113		}
   114		return headCommitID, err
   115	}

   280	// applySuggestionsToContent applies one file's suggestions bottom-up, so each edit leaves the line numbers of the
   281	// ones above it as they were (#159 AC9). Two suggestions that share a line are refused (#159 AC2).
   282	func applySuggestionsToContent(content string, edits []suggestionEdit) (string, error) {
   283		edits = slices.Clone(edits)
   284		slices.SortFunc(edits, func(a, b suggestionEdit) int { return cmp.Compare(b.comment.Line, a.comment.Line) })
   285		for i := 1; i < len(edits); i++ {
   286			if edits[i].comment.Line >= edits[i-1].startLine() {
   287				return "", ErrSuggestionOverlap
   288			}
   289		}
   290		for _, edit := range edits {
   291			var err error
   292			content, err = applySuggestionToContent(content, int(edit.comment.Line), edit.comment.SuggestionContextLines(), edit.original, edit.suggestion)
   293			if err != nil {
   294				return "", ErrSuggestionAt{Comment: edit.comment, Err: err}
   295			}
   296		}
   297		return content, nil
   298	}

   300	// startLine is the first line the suggestion replaces: its comment's line, or the start of the range it covers
   301	func (edit suggestionEdit) startLine() int64 {
   302		return edit.comment.Line - int64(strings.Count(edit.original, "\n"))
   303	}

   305	// suggestionCommitMessage is the doer's message, or the default, crediting each reviewer once (#156 AC1, #159 AC1).
   306	// The comments' posters must be loaded.
   307	func suggestionCommitMessage(comments []*issues_model.Comment, doer *user_model.User, message string) string {
   308		if strings.TrimSpace(message) == "" {
   309			if len(comments) == 1 {
   310				message = comments[0].SuggestionCommitMessage()
   311			} else {
   312				message = fmt.Sprintf("Apply %d suggestions from code review", len(comments))
   313			}
   314		}
   315		// customer question 1 on #151 is open; the spec's default: the doer authors and commits, the reviewers are credited
   316		credited := make(container.Set[int64])
   317		var trailers []string
   318		for _, comment := range comments {
   319			if comment.Poster.ID == doer.ID || comment.Poster.IsGhost() || !credited.Add(comment.Poster.ID) { // a deleted reviewer has no address to credit
   320				continue
   321			}
   322			sig := comment.Poster.NewGitSig()
   323			trailers = append(trailers, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %s <%s>", git.CoAuthoredByTrailer, sig.Name, sig.Email))
   324		}
   325		if len(trailers) == 0 {
   326			return message
   327		}
   328		return strings.TrimRight(message, "\n") + "\n\n" + strings.Join(trailers, "\n")
   329	}

   331	// applySuggestionToContent replaces line lineNum (1-based) of content with the suggestion's lines, the way
   332	// #154 draws the diff: "" deletes the line, "\n" leaves one blank line, otherwise one line per suggestion line.
   333	// original is the line the suggestion was written against, and above the lines the reviewer saw right above it;
   334	// content and both of those may use CRLF.
   335	func applySuggestionToContent(content string, lineNum int, above []string, original, suggestion string) (string, error) {
   336		lines := strings.SplitAfter(content, "\n") // every element but the last keeps its "\n"
   337		if lines[len(lines)-1] == "" {
   338			lines = lines[:len(lines)-1] // content ended with a newline
   339		}

   342			return "", ErrSuggestionOutdated
   343		}

   345		for i, want := range above {

   355			ending = "\r\n"
   356		case strings.HasSuffix(target, "\n"):
   357			ending = "\n"
   358		}

   371			}
   372			newLines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSuffix(suggestion, "\n"), "\n")
   373			replacement = strings.Join(newLines, innerEnding) + ending
   374		}
   375
   376		before := strings.Join(lines[:idx], "")
   377		if replacement == "" && ending == "" && idx > 0 {
   378			// deleting a last line that has no newline: the line before it becomes last and loses its newline,
   379			// so the file still ends without one (#156 AC11)
   380			prev := lines[idx-1]
   381			before = strings.Join(lines[:idx-1], "") + strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(prev, "\n"), "\r")
   382		}
   383		result := before + replacement + strings.Join(lines[idx+1:], "")
   384		if result == content {
   385			return "", ErrSuggestionNoChange
   386		}
   387		return result, nil
   388	}
````

    18
    19	// SuggestionOriginalLine returns the commented line as the reviewer saw it: the last line of the
    20	// stored patch, since CutDiffAroundLine stops right after the commented line.
    21	// For a multi-line comment it returns every line of the range, joined by "\n".
    22	// Old-side comments return None until #151 decides whether they may carry suggestions.
    23	func (c *Comment) SuggestionOriginalLine() optional.Option[string] {
    24		if c.Type != CommentTypeCode || c.Line <= 0 {
    25			return optional.None[string]()
    26		}
    27		if c.RangeStartLine() > 0 {
    28			lines, ok := c.RangeOriginalLines()
    29			if !ok {
    30				return optional.None[string]()
    31			}
    32			return optional.Some(strings.Join(lines, "\n"))
    33		}
    34		patch := strings.TrimRight(c.Patch, "\n")
    35		last := patch[strings.LastIndexByte(patch, '\n')+1:]
    36		if last == "" || (last[0] != '+' && last[0] != ' ') {
    37			return optional.None[string]() // "-" is the other side; "@", "d", "\\" mean no code line
    38		}
    39		return optional.Some(last[1:])
    40	}
    41
    42	// RangeOriginalLines returns lines RangeStartLine..Line of a multi-line code comment as the
    43	// reviewer saw them, false if the stored patch doesn't hold all of them.
    44	func (c *Comment) RangeOriginalLines() ([]string, bool) {
    45		start := c.RangeStartLine()
    46		if start <= 0 || c.Line < start {
    47			return nil, false
    48		}
    49		return PatchLastNewLines(c.Patch, int(c.Line-start+1))
    50	}
    51
    52	// PatchLastNewLines returns the last n new-side lines of a one-hunk patch, which end at the
    53	// commented line, skipping removed lines. False if the hunk has fewer than n.
    54	func PatchLastNewLines(patch string, n int) ([]string, bool) {
    55		rows := strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(patch, "\n"), "\n")
    56		lines := make([]string, n)
    57		for i := len(rows) - 1; i >= 0 && n > 0; i-- {
    58			switch {
    59			case rows[i] == "" || rows[i][0] == '@':
    60				return nil, false // reached the hunk header
    61			case rows[i][0] == '+' || rows[i][0] == ' ':
    62				n--
    63				lines[n] = rows[i][1:]
    64			}
    65		}
    66		return lines, n == 0
    67	}
    68
    69	// SuggestionContextLines returns the new-side lines the stored patch shows above the commented line, in file
    70	// order. Applying a suggestion checks them too, since blame-based invalidation can miss the commented line
    71	// moving onto an identical one, like another "}" (#156 AC3).
    72	func (c *Comment) SuggestionContextLines() []string {
    73		if !c.SuggestionOriginalLine().Has() {
    74			return nil
    75		}
    76		lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(c.Patch, "\n"), "\n")
    77		hunkStart := -1
    78		for i, line := range lines {
    79			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "@@") {
    80				hunkStart = i
    81			}
    82		}
    83		if hunkStart < 0 {
    84			return nil
    85		}
    86		var above []string
    87		for _, line := range lines[hunkStart+1 : len(lines)-1] { // the last line is the commented one
    88			if line != "" && (line[0] == ' ' || line[0] == '+') {
    89				above = append(above, line[1:])
    90			} // "-" is the old side, "\" is "No newline at end of file"
    91		}
    92		return above
    93	}

    97	func (c *Comment) SuggestionBlocks(ctx context.Context) []string {
    98		return markdown.FencedCodeBlocks(ctx, []byte(c.Content), "suggestion")
    99	}

// UnsignedLine returns the LOC of the code comment without + or -
func (c *Comment) UnsignedLine() uint64 {
	if c.Line < 0 {
		return uint64(c.Line * -1)
	}
	return uint64(c.Line)
}

// RangeStartLine returns the first line of a multi-line code comment, or 0 for a single-line one
func (c *Comment) RangeStartLine() int64 {
	if c.CommentMetaData == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return c.CommentMetaData.StartLine
}

// CodeCommentLink returns the url to a comment in code
func (c *Comment) CodeCommentLink(ctx context.Context) string {
	err := c.LoadIssue(ctx)
	if err != nil { // Silently dropping errors :unamused:
		log.Error("LoadIssue(%d): %v", c.IssueID, err)
		return ""
	}
	err = c.Issue.LoadRepo(ctx)
	if err != nil { // Silently dropping errors :unamused:
		log.Error("loadRepo(%d): %v", c.Issue.RepoID, err)
		return ""
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s/files#%s", c.Issue.Link(), c.HashTag())
}

// MetaCloseReason returns the reason recorded on a close comment; comments without metadata have none.
// The duplicate target is not included: load it with LoadCloseDuplicateIssue.

```text
// The suggestions picked to apply together (#159). The batch lives only in this page, so a reload empties it (AC4).
type BatchItem = {id: string, path: string, start: number, end: number, message: string, toggle: HTMLElement};
const batch = new Map<string, BatchItem>();
let batchBar: {el: HTMLElement, count: HTMLElement, message: HTMLInputElement, edited: boolean} | null = null;

// a suggestion whose comment was deleted, or edited so it no longer offers one, has lost its toggle from the page and
// can't be applied, so it leaves the batch; true if any did
function dropRemovedFromBatch(): boolean {
  let dropped = false;
  for (const [id, item] of batch) {
    if (!item.toggle.isConnected) {
      batch.delete(id);
      dropped = true;
    }
  }
  return dropped;
}

// not batch.values().some(): Iterator helpers need Safari 18.4 / Firefox 131, newer than the es2020 build target
function overlapsBatch(item: BatchItem): boolean {
  for (const other of batch.values()) {
    if (other.path === item.path && other.start <= item.end && item.start <= other.end) return true;
  }
  return false;
}

// The default message matches ApplySuggestions' on the server, and is the suggestion's own for one (AC1, AC11)
function batchMessage(): string {
  if (batch.size === 1) return batch.values().next().value!.message;
  return `Apply ${batch.size} suggestions from code review`;
}
```

````text
func TestApplySuggestionsToContent(t *testing.T) {
	edit := func(line int64, original, suggestion string) suggestionEdit {
		return suggestionEdit{
			comment:    &issues_model.Comment{Type: issues_model.CommentTypeCode, Line: line, TreePath: "main.go", Patch: "@@ -1,1 +1,1 @@\n+" + original},
			original:   original,
			suggestion: suggestion,
		}
	}
	const content = "l1\nl2\nl3\nl4\nl5\nl6\n"

	t.Run("AC9 one line becomes three above, a line deleted below: the same as applying them one at a time", func(t *testing.T) {
		got, err := applySuggestionsToContent(content, []suggestionEdit{edit(2, "l2", "a\nb\nc\n"), edit(5, "l5", "")})
		require.NoError(t, err)
		assert.Equal(t, "l1\na\nb\nc\nl3\nl4\nl6\n", got)
		// the order the suggestions were selected in doesn't matter
		got, err = applySuggestionsToContent(content, []suggestionEdit{edit(5, "l5", ""), edit(2, "l2", "a\nb\nc\n")})
		require.NoError(t, err)
		assert.Equal(t, "l1\na\nb\nc\nl3\nl4\nl6\n", got)
	})

	t.Run("neighbouring lines both apply", func(t *testing.T) {
		got, err := applySuggestionsToContent(content, []suggestionEdit{edit(3, "l3", "x\n"), edit(4, "l4", "y\n")})
		require.NoError(t, err)
		assert.Equal(t, "l1\nl2\nx\ny\nl5\nl6\n", got)
	})

	t.Run("AC2 two suggestions on the same line overlap", func(t *testing.T) {
		_, err := applySuggestionsToContent(content, []suggestionEdit{edit(3, "l3", "x\n"), edit(3, "l3", "y\n")})
		assert.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrSuggestionOverlap)
	})

	t.Run("AC2 a range that covers another suggestion's line overlaps", func(t *testing.T) {
		_, err := applySuggestionsToContent(content, []suggestionEdit{edit(4, "l3\nl4", "x\n"), edit(3, "l3", "y\n")})
		assert.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrSuggestionOverlap)
	})

	t.Run("AC3 an outdated suggestion is named", func(t *testing.T) {
		_, err := applySuggestionsToContent(content, []suggestionEdit{edit(2, "l2", "x\n"), edit(5, "changed", "y\n")})
		var at ErrSuggestionAt
		require.ErrorAs(t, err, &at)
		assert.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrSuggestionOutdated)
		assert.EqualValues(t, 5, at.Comment.Line)
	})
}

func TestApplySuggestion(t *testing.T) {
````

````text
// fileLines returns "l1\n".."lN\n" with the given lines replaced
func fileLines(n int, replace map[int]string) string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	for i := 1; i <= n; i++ {
		if s, ok := replace[i]; ok {
			sb.WriteString(s + "\n")
		} else {
			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "l%d\n", i)
		}
	}
	return sb.String()
}
````

````markdown
# #189 (S6a) — apply a suggestion across several lines: spec revision + PR

## Context

controlled-opposition's spec review on #189 (Nov 17) asked for four changes before coding:
reconcile AC7 with the planned signature change, say whether the range check keeps S3's
lines-above check, add ACs for unreadable original lines and for a suggestion in a reply on a range
thread, and put the issue on the `Sprint 3` milestone. #158 (S5, PR #177) and #159 (S6, PR #196)
have both merged, so coding is unblocked.

What's on `main` already does most of the work:
- `Comment.SuggestionOriginalLine()` returns a range's lines joined by `\n`, or None when they
  can't be read back ([comment_suggestion.go:23](models/issues/comment_suggestion.go#L23)).
- `suggestionEdit.startLine()` and the batch overlap check already handle ranges
  ([suggestion.go:286-303](services/repository/files/suggestion.go#L286-L303)), and so does the
  frontend batch ([suggestion.ts:192](web_src/js/markup/suggestion.ts#L192)).
- Replies already inherit their thread's range ([review.go:295](services/pull/review.go#L295)).
- The only blockers are the guard at [suggestion.go:140](services/repository/files/suggestion.go#L140),
  `applySuggestionToContent` comparing one line, and `(not .RangeStartLine)` in two templates.

**Deadline flag:** today is Nov 20, and the sprint closed Nov 19 at 11:59 PM (2-hour grace, then
−10%/day). The PR also needs a teammate's approval on its latest commit before merging.

## Step 1 — revise the #189 spec (draft in `drafts-issue-189/`; you post it, since `gh` isn't installed)

- **AC3** adds: "…or any line the stored snippet shows above line L no longer matches (S3's
  moved-onto-identical check)." That answers the lines-above question: **kept**.
- **AC7** rewritten: "S3's `TestApplySuggestionToContent` cases pass with their inputs, expected
  results and call unchanged." This holds as written, because the signature doesn't change (see
  the Design Decision below).
- **New AC9:** "Given a range comment whose original lines can't be read back from its stored
  snippet, then no Apply button is shown, and a direct POST gets 404, as S3 AC7 does for a comment
  with no applicable suggestion."
- **New AC10:** "Given a suggestion posted as a reply in a range thread (lines L–M), when it's
  applied, then it replaces lines L–M, as AC1 does."
- **Design Decision** reworded:
  - `applySuggestionToContent` keeps its signature. A range is passed as a multi-line `original`,
    with `lineNum` as its last line and the start inferred from the line count, as
    `suggestionEdit.startLine()` already does.
  - The alternative that lost is an explicit `startLine` parameter, which would change every S3
    test call.
  - `SuggestionContextLines()` returns only the lines above L.
- **Scope** stays small. Fix "S3's Apply attribute" in the justification to say both templates.
- **Reply to the review** (in your own words): one line for each of the four requested changes.
  You add the milestone in the GitHub UI.

## Step 2 — branch and code

`git switch main && git pull origin main && git switch -c feat/issue-189-range-apply`

1. [suggestion.go](services/repository/files/suggestion.go)
   - Delete the range guard (lines 140–142).
   - Generalise `applySuggestionToContent`, keeping its signature:
     - `want := append(slices.Clip(above), strings.Split(original, "\n")...)`. The first checked
       index is `lineNum - len(want)`, and the first replaced index is `start = lineNum - n`.
     - One loop compares every wanted line, trimming `\r`/`\n` as the current above-loop does. It
       replaces both the above-loop and the single-target compare.
     - `ending` comes from the last line of the range.
     - `before` is `lines[:start]`. The no-final-newline deletion case uses `lines[start-1]`.
     - `result = before + replacement + lines[lineNum:]`.
   - Update the doc comment: "line(s) ending at lineNum".
2. [comment_suggestion.go](models/issues/comment_suggestion.go): in `SuggestionContextLines`, when
   `RangeStartLine() > 0`, drop the range's own `Line-start` lines from the tail, so callers get
   only the lines above L.
3. Delete `(not .RangeStartLine)` in [comments.tmpl:61](templates/repo/diff/comments.tmpl#L61) and
   [conversation.tmpl:98](templates/repo/issue/view_content/conversation.tmpl#L98).

No router, JS, locale or schema change. The existing messages and status codes cover every AC.

## Step 3 — tests (expected values taken from the ACs)

- `TestApplySuggestionToContent`: add range rows covering:
  - AC1: lines 2–4 replaced, lines before and after untouched.
  - AC2: an empty block, and one blank line.
  - AC3: the first, middle or last line changed; the file shorter than M; a line above L changed.
  - AC5: a CRLF file, and a range ending on a last line with no final newline, including deleting
    it.
  - AC6: no change.

  Existing rows stay byte-for-byte as they are (AC7).
- `TestApplySuggestionsToContent`: add AC8, a range and a non-overlapping single line in one file.
- `TestCommentSuggestionContextLines`: add a range case that excludes the range's own lines.
- `TestApplySuggestion`:
  - Flip "a range suggestion until #189" into a range comment that gets past the applicability
    checks (a stale head gives `ErrSuggestionHeadMoved`).
  - Add AC9: StartLine 1 on the 2-line hunk gives `ErrSuggestionNotApplicable`.
  - Run the `cannotApply` loop for a range comment too (AC4: 403 and closed/merged).
- `pull_review_range_test.go`:
  - Flip the "no Apply on range" subtest to "range has Apply" (AC4, both pages).
  - Append an end-to-end subtest that posts a range suggestion on lines 11–13, applies it, and
    checks that README lines 11–13 were replaced and nothing else changed (AC1). It goes last,

- AC10 evidence: S5's existing reply-inherits-range test plus the AC1 apply test. Check that S5's
  test exists in `services/pull/review_range_test.go`; if it doesn't, add a reply POST to the
````

```text
// line. original is the line(s) the suggestion was written against, one per "\n" for a range (#189), and above the
// lines the reviewer saw right above them; content and both of those may use CRLF.
func applySuggestionToContent(content string, lineNum int, above []string, original, suggestion string) (string, error) {
	lines := strings.SplitAfter(content, "\n") // every element but the last keeps its "\n"
	if lines[len(lines)-1] == "" {
		lines = lines[:len(lines)-1] // content ended with a newline
	}
	want := append(slices.Clip(above), strings.Split(original, "\n")...)
	first := lineNum - len(want) // index of the first line checked
	start := first + len(above)  // index of the first line replaced
	if first < 0 || lineNum > len(lines) { // also refuses lineNum < 1, and lines that moved too near the top
		return "", ErrSuggestionOutdated
	}
	// blame-based invalidation misses a line that moved onto an identical one, like another "}"; its neighbours don't
	for i, w := range want {
		if strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(lines[first+i], "\n"), "\r") != strings.TrimSuffix(w, "\r") {
			return "", ErrSuggestionOutdated
		}
	}

	target := lines[lineNum-1] // the last line replaced decides the ending, so a final line without one keeps it
	ending := ""
	switch {
	case strings.HasSuffix(target, "\r\n"):
		ending = "\r\n"
	case strings.HasSuffix(target, "\n"):
		ending = "\n"
	}

	var replacement string
	if suggestion != "" {
		innerEnding := ending
		if innerEnding == "" { // the last line has no newline, so new lines in between take the file's own
			innerEnding = "\n"
			if strings.Contains(content, "\r\n") {
				innerEnding = "\r\n"
			}
		}
		newLines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSuffix(suggestion, "\n"), "\n")
		replacement = strings.Join(newLines, innerEnding) + ending
	}

	before := strings.Join(lines[:start], "")
	if replacement == "" && ending == "" && start > 0 {
		// deleting a last line that has no newline: the line before it becomes last and loses its newline,
		// so the file still ends without one (#156 AC11)
		prev := lines[start-1]
		before = strings.Join(lines[:start-1], "") + strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(prev, "\n"), "\r")
	}
	result := before + replacement + strings.Join(lines[lineNum:], "")
	if result == content {
		return "", ErrSuggestionNoChange
	}
	return result, nil
}
```

```text
Closes #159

## What changed

A PR author can now pick several suggestions and apply them as one commit. Each suggestion that has an Apply button also gets **Add to batch**. Once something is in the batch, a bar at the bottom of the page shows "N suggestions selected", an editable commit message and **Apply suggestions**.

- **Service (`services/repository/files/suggestion.go`):** new `ApplySuggestions(ctx, doer, pr, comments, expectedHeadSHA, message)`. S3's `ApplySuggestion` is now a one-element call to it, so single Apply runs the same checks and keeps #156's and #157's messages.
  - Before anything is committed, it checks:
    - the batch size (at most 50) and duplicate IDs;
    - each comment's S3 checks and S4's already-applied check;
    - push permission and the head commit (once for the batch);
    - branch protection (per file);
    - outdated comments.
  - It reads each file once, applies that file's suggestions bottom-up so earlier edits don't shift later line numbers, and refuses two suggestions that share a line. Then it makes one `ChangeRepoFiles` commit with one entry per file, and marks every suggestion applied with that commit (S4's `MarkSuggestionApplied`; a failed save is logged, as in S4).
  - Default message: one suggestion keeps S3's "Apply suggestion from @x on file"; several get "Apply N suggestions from code review". Each reviewer other than the applier gets one `Co-authored-by` trailer.
  - A refusal caused by one suggestion is wrapped in `ErrSuggestionAt`, so the page can say which one, e.g. "… already been applied. (README.md:4)".
- **Web:**
  - New route `POST …/files/reviews/comments/apply` that takes `comment_ids`, `head_commit_id` and `message`, reusing S3's form.
  - New `ApplySuggestions` handler. It refuses more than 50 IDs before looking any of them up, so a long list can't cost a query per ID.
  - `applySuggestionError` maps the new errors to 400s and appends `(path:line)` for a named suggestion.
  - New locale strings.
- **Templates:** the two comment templates add the batch data attributes inside the existing Apply condition, so a suggestion with no Apply (no push access, closed PR, outdated, already applied, a range) gets no batch button either. The limit comes from `files_service.MaxSuggestionBatch`.
- **Frontend (`web_src/js/markup/suggestion.ts`):**
  - **Add to batch / Remove from batch** sits next to Apply, and keeps its label when an edited comment is re-rendered.
  - The batch is held only in the page.
  - An overlapping suggestion, or a 51st, is refused with a toast.
  - The bottom bar posts the batch and reloads.
  - S3's POST-and-reload code moved into a shared `postApply`.
- **After the #196 review:**
  - A suggestion whose comment was deleted, or edited so it no longer offers one, is dropped from the batch when Apply is clicked. The bar shows what is left instead of posting a batch that would fail.
  - The overlap check is a plain loop. `Iterator.prototype.some` needs Safari 18.4 / Firefox 131, newer than the build target.
  - The batch integration test waits for the pull request's background update after each apply. A comment posted 39 ms after an apply got a 500 on MySQL CI.
- **Merge with `main`:** S4 (#157) landed in the same function while this was open. Its already-applied check now lives in the per-suggestion checks, and its marking runs for every suggestion in the commit.

## Why

Applying suggestions one at a time adds a commit per suggestion. #159 asks for one commit. This covers #159 AC1–AC14. AC15 (a range suggestion in a batch) waits for #189, which makes ranges applicable.

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1: one commit with all the selected suggestions, each marked applied with it; default message "Apply N suggestions from code review"; each reviewer credited | `TestPullReviewApplySuggestions/AC1_AC9_*` (one commit, its parent is the old head, the default message with one trailer, both comments store that commit and the applier); `TestSuggestionCommitMessage` (N default, distinct trailers in order, applier and Ghost skipped); `suggestion.test.ts › AC1 Apply posts every suggestion…`, `› AC1 AC11 the message…` | unit, integration | AC |
| AC2: overlapping suggestions refused, in the page and on a direct POST | `TestApplySuggestionsToContent/AC2_*` (same line, a range covering a line); `TestApplySuggestion/AC2_*`; `TestApplySuggestionError/#159_AC2_*`; `TestPullReviewApplySuggestions/AC2_*`; `suggestion.test.ts › AC2 …` | unit, integration | AC |
```

```markdown
### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: small` · Type: Feature · Part of #151 · Depends on #156 (S3, merged in #179) and #158 (S5, merged in #177)

As a PR author, I want to apply a reviewer's suggestion on a range of lines with one click, so
that multi-line feedback lands on my branch the same way single-line feedback does.

### User Scenario

Ana selects lines 18–22 of `main.go` and suggests replacing them with two lines (S5). Ben clicks
**Apply suggestion**, keeps the default message "Apply suggestion from @ana on main.go" and
confirms. The page reloads, and the PR has one more commit in which lines 18–22 are replaced by
Ana's two lines and nothing else in the file changed.

### Acceptance Criteria

Errors from the Apply POST are returned as in S3 (#156): HTTP 400 with the message shown on the
page, unless an AC says otherwise.

- [ ] AC1: Given a suggestion on lines L–M (S5) and a user who can push to the head branch, when
  they apply it, then exactly one commit is added that replaces lines L–M with the block's lines
  in order, matching S5 AC5's diff. No line before L or after M changes. The commit message
  follows S3 AC1 (default "Apply suggestion from @<reviewer> on <file>", editable).
- [ ] AC2: Given the block is empty or holds one blank line, when it is applied, then the commit
  deletes lines L–M, or replaces them with one blank line (S5 AC6, S3 AC12).
- [ ] AC3: Given any line in L–M (first, middle or last) differs at head from the line the
  suggestion was written against, or a line the stored snippet shows above L differs (S3's check
  for code that moved onto identical text, like another `}`), or the file now has fewer than M
  lines, or it was deleted or renamed, when someone applies it, then nothing is committed and they
  see "This suggestion is outdated: the code changed since it was written."
- [ ] AC4: Given a range suggestion, then the Apply button is shown or hidden under the same
  conditions as a single-line one (S3 AC2, AC5, AC7, AC9), and a direct POST gets S3's responses:
  403 for a user who can't push, 400 "Suggestions can only be applied to an open pull request
  whose branch still exists." for a closed or merged PR, 400 "This branch has new commits since
  the page was loaded. Reload the page and try again." for a stale head, and `Cannot commit to
  protected branch "<branch>".` for a protected branch.
- [ ] AC5: Given a file with CRLF line endings or no final newline, including a range that ends
  on the last line, when a range suggestion is applied, then the new lines use the file's line
  ending and the file's final-newline state is unchanged (S3 AC11).
- [ ] AC6: Given a range suggestion whose block equals lines L–M, when applied, then nothing is
  committed and they see "This suggestion makes no changes to the code." (S3 AC10).
- [ ] AC7: Given a single-line suggestion, then applying it behaves exactly as before: S3's
  `TestApplySuggestionToContent` cases keep their inputs, expected results and call unchanged and
  pass, as do S3's other tests. *Reworded after the spec review.*
- [ ] AC8: Given a range suggestion and a single-line suggestion in the same file that don't overlap, when both are applied in one batch (S6, #159), then the commit applies each exactly as AC1 and S3 AC1 would on their own. *Moved from #159 AC15.*
- [ ] AC9: Given a range comment whose original lines can't be read back from its stored snippet
  (S5's `RangeOriginalLines()` returns false), then no Apply button is shown, and a direct POST
  gets 404, as S3 AC7 does for a comment with no applicable suggestion. *Added after the spec
  review.*
- [ ] AC10: Given a suggestion posted as a reply in a range thread on lines L–M (S5 makes the
  reply inherit the range), when it is applied, then it replaces lines L–M, as AC1 does. *Added
  after the spec review.*

### Out of Scope

- Applying several suggestions in one commit (S6, #159), which reuses this.
- Recording "applied" (S4, #157) and the API (S7, #160).
- Re-anchoring a range whose lines moved but didn't change: it is refused as outdated, like S3.

### Open Questions

- None.

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Generalise S3's `applySuggestionToContent` in
`services/repository/files/suggestion.go` to replace the lines that end at `lineNum` and number
as many as the original has, keeping its signature. A range comment passes S5's
`SuggestionOriginalLine()`, which already joins lines L–M with `"\n"`. Every one of those lines,
plus the lines above L, is checked before replacing. `SuggestionContextLines()` returns only the
lines above L for a range, so the check doesn't count the range's own lines as context.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *An explicit start-line parameter on `applySuggestionToContent`.* Clearer at the call site, but
  every S3 test call would change. That is the conflict the spec review raised against AC7. S6
  already infers a range's start from the original's line count (`suggestionEdit.startLine()`), so
  a second source for the same number could disagree with it.
- *A separate `applyRangeSuggestionToContent`.* Leaves S3's function untouched, but duplicates its
  CRLF, final-newline and outdated handling, so the two would drift apart.
- *Build a patch from S5's rendered diff and run `git apply` in a temp clone.* S3 already rejected
  this: fuzzy matching can land the change on the wrong lines, and it duplicates what
  `ChangeRepoFiles` does.

**Rationale:** One function keeps a single place for line-ending handling. An unchanged signature
lets S3's tests serve as the single-line regression check (AC7) without editing them, and the
range's start comes from the same place S6's overlap check already reads it.

**Consequences:** S6 (#159) already calls it per suggestion, bottom-up, so a batch can hold ranges
with no change to S6. A range that moved but didn't change is refused. For a range, S5 stores the
whole hunk above L, not S3's few context lines. So the lines-above check covers more lines: an
unrelated in-place edit higher up in the same hunk also makes the suggestion outdated.

### Scope

small

### Scope Justification

One service function in `services/repository/files/suggestion.go` (range replace plus a range
outdated check), a one-line change to `SuggestionContextLines()`, and S3's Apply attribute offered
on range comments in the two comment templates (`templates/repo/diff/comments.tmpl`,
`templates/repo/issue/view_content/conversation.tmpl`). Unit tests cover AC1–AC3, AC5, AC6, AC8
and AC9, and integration cases cover AC1 and AC4. No new route, UI or schema change.

---
_Drafted with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) for @Jack-Donohue; revised after @controlled-opposition's spec review._
```

```markdown
Closes #189

## What changed

A suggestion on a range of lines (S5, #158) can now be applied like a single-line one, on its own
or in a batch (S6, #159).

- **Service (`services/repository/files/suggestion.go`):**
  - Removed the guard that refused range comments until this issue.
  - `applySuggestionToContent` keeps its signature. `original` can now hold several lines joined
    by `"\n"`: the range ends at `lineNum`, and its start is that minus the line count, as #159's
    `suggestionEdit.startLine()` already worked it out.
  - One loop checks the lines above the range and every line in it, then replaces them all.
  - The last line of the range sets the line ending, so a range that ends on a last line with no
    final newline keeps the file ending without one.
- **Model (`models/issues/comment_suggestion.go`):** for a range, `SuggestionContextLines()` drops
  the range's own lines and returns only the lines above L. Before, those lines would have been
  checked twice, once as context and once as the original.
- **Templates:** removed `(not .RangeStartLine)` from the Apply condition in `diff/comments.tmpl`
  and `issue/view_content/conversation.tmpl`. Range suggestions now get Apply, and with it
  **Add to batch**.
- No route, JS, locale or schema change. The batch frontend and the overlap check already handled
  ranges.

## Why

#177 shipped range suggestions without an Apply button because applying them was left to this
issue. This covers #189 AC1–AC10. The spec was revised after @controlled-opposition's review
(AC3, AC7, AC9 and AC10).

## Test Evidence

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** For a range, S5 stores the whole hunk above L (`window = math.MaxInt32` in
`services/pull/review.go`), and the lines-above check uses all of it. An in-place edit higher up
in the same hunk therefore makes a range suggestion outdated, while S3 only checks a few lines.
The fix is to trim S5's stored range snippet, which is already flagged with a `shortcut:` comment
there.

**Encountered:** `make 'test-integration#<regex>'` passes the pattern to `sh` unquoted, so a regex
with `(` or `|` fails with a syntax error. I ran `go test -run` directly instead.
```

Base directory for this skill: /home/vscode/.claude/plugins/cache/ponytail/ponytail/5.3.3/skills/ponytail-review

Review a change like the senior developer who will be paged when it breaks.
Order of importance: correct, safe, holds under load, tested, fast, lean.
Lean still matters: every extra line must be read, tested and fixed later.
This is a report the user asked for, so give it in full.

## 1. Understand first

- Review what the user names: uncommitted or staged changes, a branch, a PR
  link, or files. Nothing named: the uncommitted changes, or the last commit
  if there are none.
- Read the diff, then the code it touches: callers of every changed function,
  the functions it calls, the tests, the README.
- Trace the real flow: where data comes in, what is stored, what goes out.
- A change can break code it does not touch. When a signature, return value
  or behavior changes, grep every caller.
- Find the expected load in the repo (README, deploy config): one person
  running a script, or many users and processes at once. Judge scale against
  that, and say which load you assumed.

## 2. Look for

1. **Bug:** wrong result, crash, missed edge case (empty, zero, last item,
   rounding, time zones), a caller broken by the change, a fix applied in one
   caller while the shared function stays broken.
2. **Risk:** security holes (injection, weak randomness, secrets, missing
   checks on input from users), data loss (errors swallowed, writes in the
   wrong order, no transaction).
3. **Scale:** fine for one user, wrong for many: check-then-write races, the
   same work done by every process, memory or lists that only grow, a query
   per item, O(n^2) on big input, per-process state that must be shared.
4. **Missing test:** risky new logic (a branch, a parser, money, security,
   data writes, a bug fix) with no test that fails when it breaks. One good
   test, not coverage.
5. **Speed:** big slowdowns are problems. Small wins (work repeated in a hot
   loop) are suggestions; some software counts every millisecond.
6. **Lean:** code that should not exist or should be smaller.
   - delete: dead code, unused options, speculative features
   - reuse: the repo already has this helper (name the path)
   - stdlib / native: the standard library or platform already does it; a
     new dependency for a few lines
   - yagni: abstraction with one implementation, config nobody sets
   - merge: near-copies that must change together
   - split: one function doing several unrelated jobs, so it is hard to read
     or test. Split by job, never by line count, and never into helpers that
     exist only to make a function shorter.

## 3. Check before you report

- Every finding needs a concrete case: "this input or situation leads to this
  wrong result". No case, no finding.
- Re-read the lines and confirm: the caller exists, the value can really be
  empty, the code really is unused.
- A shortcut marked with a `shortcut:` (or older `ponytail:`) comment that names its limit is a
  decision, not a finding, unless the expected load already crosses it.
- Propose the smallest fix that works. Prefer fixes that delete code. Never
  add layers, frameworks or config the problem does not need.
- No style taste, no "consider", no vague worries.

## 4. Output

Very simple English: short sentences, everyday words. Explain a technical
term the first time you use it. The reader may never have seen this code.

Start with `What this change does:` in two or three sentences.

Then the findings in three groups, skip empty groups:
- **Must fix:** bug, security, data loss, breaks at the expected load.
- **Should fix:** risky code without a test, real slowness, duplication, a
  function that mixes jobs, code that should not exist.
- **Nice to have:** small speed-ups, shorter forms.

Number findings across all groups, so the user can say "fix 2 and 5".
Every finding has all four parts, each one or two short sentences:

2. **Orders land on the wrong day** (`billing/close_day.py:L40-52`)
   - **What this is:** At midnight this job closes the day and bills all orders of that day.
   - **Problem:** It takes "today" from the server clock, which runs in UTC. An order placed
     at 00:30 in Berlin is billed on the day before.
   - **Fix:** Compute the day once in the shop's time zone:
     `datetime.now(ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin")).date()`. One line, nothing else changes.
   - **If we skip it:** Late orders show the wrong date, and accounting fixes them by hand.

End with:
- `Verdict: Ship.` or `Verdict: fix 1 and 3 first.`
- `Lean: -<N> lines possible.` when lean findings exist.
- `Not checked:` one line, if something mattered and you could not check it.

Nothing found: `What this change does:`, then `Looks good. Ship.` and one line
on what you checked.

Lists findings, changes no code.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-20 02:09:52Z)**_

**What this change does:** It lets reviewers' suggestions that span several lines (L–M) be applied, alone or in a batch. The function that rewrites the file now checks and replaces every line of the range plus the lines shown above it, while keeping its signature. The model returns only the lines above the range, and the two comment templates no longer hide Apply on ranges.

I assumed the course fork's load: a few users on one Gitea instance. Nothing here touches shared state or runs in a loop over many items.

What I checked and found fine:
- **Every caller:** only the two web handlers ([pull_review.go:185](routers/web/repo/pull_review.go#L185), [pull_review.go:236](routers/web/repo/pull_review.go#L236)) reach this code, and both are covered by tests.
- **The stored snippet:** it always ends on the commented line ([diff.go:175](modules/git/diff.go#L175) stops right after it). So the trimming in `SuggestionContextLines` lines up with how `PatchLastNewLines` reads the range, and it can't go out of bounds once `SuggestionOriginalLine().Has()` is true.
- **Batch overlap:** with ranges sorted by their last line, comparing each one to the next is enough, nested ranges included. Applying bottom-up means a lower range's check never sees an upper range's changes.
- **Empty file, line 0, file shorter than M:** each is refused as outdated.
- **Stale comments:** no code comment still says ranges can't be applied.

**Should fix**

1. **A range is refused as outdated because of an edit far above it** ([comment_suggestion.go:92-94](models/issues/comment_suggestion.go#L92-L94))
   - **What this is:** Before applying, the code checks that the lines above the range still read as they did when the reviewer wrote the suggestion. This catches code that moved onto identical text.
   - **Problem:** For ranges, S5 stores the whole diff hunk above L, not S3's 4 lines, so every one of those lines must still match. Example: a hunk covers lines 1–40, a reviewer suggests on 38–40, and the author fixes a typo on line 5 without adding lines. The comment is not marked outdated and the Apply button shows, but clicking it says "This suggestion is outdated."
   - **Fix:** In the same `if`, keep only the last `setting.UI.CodeCommentLines` lines: `above = above[max(0, len(above)-setting.UI.CodeCommentLines):]`. That's one line, and `models/issues` already imports `setting`. Add one model test case, change AC3's wording to "the same lines above L that S3 checks", and drop the "Introduced" Tech Debt item from the PR.
   - **If we skip it:** Authors of PRs with large hunks get "outdated" on suggestions that are fine and have to copy them by hand. It's already listed in the PR's Tech Debt, so it's a known, documented limit, not a hidden one.

Verdict: Ship. Finding 1 is optional, a few minutes of work, and lets you delete a Tech Debt item.

Not checked: MySQL/Postgres, the full integration suite, and a manual run in the browser. The team's `docs/sprint3/report.md` still shows #189 and #159 as "⬜ PENDING", so it needs updating before the deadline.

```text
> 1. **The PR closes [S6. Apply several suggestions in one commit #159](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/159), but AC15 isn't done.** The description says AC15 waits for [S6a. Apply a suggestion across several lines #189](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/189) (still open), but `Closes #159` will close the issue on merge with AC15 unchecked and nothing tracking it except [S6a. Apply a suggestion across several lines #189](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/189)'s own scope. Either change it to `Part of #159`, or move AC15 into [S6a. Apply a suggestion across several lines #189](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/189) (or a linked follow-up) on the issue before merging. The issue body also still has `#S6A` placeholders where [S6a. Apply a suggestion across several lines #189](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/189) belongs.
> 2. **AI Assistance comment for the implementation.** [S6. Apply several suggestions in one commit #159](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/159)'s only AI Assistance comment covers the spec revision (`2026-11-17_claude-code_issue-159-spec.md`). Please post one for this implementation's log so the PR's pointer leads somewhere.
> 3. **A deleted or edited comment gets stuck in the batch.** `batch` (`suggestion.ts:104`) is only changed by the toggle. Add A and B, then delete B, or edit B so it has no suggestion or two. The re-render shows no toggle for B, but B's ID is still in the batch. Every **Apply suggestions** then posts it, the server answers a bare 404 (comment not found, or `ErrSuggestionNotApplicable`), and the bar shows only "An error occurred". There's no way to remove B except reloading, and nothing tells the user that. Dropping entries whose element is gone when the bar is used (or when a comment re-renders without a toggle), or naming the suggestion on a 404 (see 5), would fix it. A Vitest case for this would go with the existing re-render test.
>
> **Optional**
>
> 4. **`batch.values().some(...)` (`suggestion.ts:177`) needs Iterator helpers.** Iterator helpers are ES2025, the build targets es2020 (`vite.config.ts:74`) with no polyfill, and this is the first use in `web_src`. On Safari before 18.4 or Firefox before 131 it throws a `TypeError`, so a second suggestion can't be added. Vitest runs on Node, which has them, so the tests can't catch it. `[...batch.values()].some(...)` costs nothing.
> 5. **Some refusals still aren't named.** `ErrSuggestionNotApplicable` and a missing comment come back as a bare 404, and `ErrSuggestionOverlap` doesn't say which pair overlaps. For a batch of several, "An error occurred" leaves the user guessing which one to remove. Wrapping these in `ErrSuggestionAt` like the outdated and applied cases, and answering a JSON 400 for a batch, would match AC3/AC10's naming.
> 6. **One query per comment ID.** The handler calls `GetCommentByID` for each ID, and the service then loads each comment's review and poster one at a time, which is about 150 queries for a full batch of 50. One `db.Find` with `In("id", ids)` and `CommentList.LoadPosters` would cut that to a few. The limit-before-lookup check is a good guard either way.
> 7. **The ` (path:line)` suffix is appended after translation** (`pull_review.go:249`), so translators can't place or punctuate it. The plural-free "N suggestions selected" label is already under Tech Debt. A `%s` variant of the three named messages would fix this one the same way.
>
> Generalising S3's service so single Apply runs through the same checks was the right call: S4's applied check and marking now cover both paths for free, and applying each file's edits bottom-up keeps line drift out of the picture.
>
> — [@vvchopra](https://github.com/vvchopra), review drafted with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5); I read the diff and ran the tests listed above myself.
```
